data.title: SSH Authorized Keys Modifiable Without Detection
data.summary:
Public keys were added to user and service account authorized_keys files on Unix hosts,
granting durable access that survived password changes and was not detected or reviewed.
data.description:
An added public key is persistence that outlives the credential compromise that enabled
it. Password rotation does not revoke it, the subsequent logins are legitimate
authentications, and nothing distinguishes them from the account's normal use.

Service accounts are the preferred target: they are rarely reviewed, frequently permit key
authentication, and often exist on many hosts with the same name, so one key placed widely
provides estate-wide access.

The files are small, change rarely, and are easy to monitor, which makes this another case
where the control is cheap and simply absent.
data.recommendation:
* Monitor authorized_keys files for modification and alert on changes outside configuration
  management.
* Manage keys through configuration management so the authoritative set is declared and
  drift is visible.
* Review keys on service accounts specifically, and disable key authentication for accounts
  that do not require it.
* Prefer short-lived certificates over long-lived authorized keys where the platform
  supports it.
data.short_recommendation: Manage authorized_keys through configuration management and alert on drift.
